stories.headline: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid scandal; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
stories.title: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid scandal; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
stories.summary: NVIDIA co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his roles as President, CEO, and board member, effective immediately, following reports of extramarital affairs. The company's board has appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while initiating a search for a permanent successor. Harvey C. Jones, a veteran board member, was also named as the company's first-ever chair of the board. NVIDIA stated that despite the leadership change and market volatility, its business operations, order book, and product roadmap remain unchanged.
facts: Jensen Huang resigned as President, CEO, and board member on November 12, 2026.
CFO Colette Kress was appointed as interim CEO.
Harvey C. Jones was appointed as the first-ever Chair of the Board.
The resignation follows reports of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy.
NVIDIA's board has started a search for a permanent successor.
The company stated that its business operations and product roadmap will continue without interruption.
limitations_or_qualifiers: The leadership transition is currently interim; a permanent CEO has not been selected.
The resignation occurred amid significant stock market volatility.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a massive shift for the company central to the global AI hardware supply chain and the broader artificial intelligence economy.

editorial_case.new_development: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of NVIDIA, with CFO Colette Kress taking over the role on an interim basis.
editorial_case.affected_listener: Investors, AI hardware buyers, and industry partners who rely on NVIDIA's stability are directly affected.
editorial_case.why_today: The resignation and board announcement occurred today, marking the most significant leadership shift in the history of the AI hardware industry.
editorial_case.distinct_question: What does a post-Jensen Huang NVIDIA mean for the long-term AI infrastructure roadmap?
editorial_case.new_since_prior_coverage: This is an immediate, confirmed leadership change following earlier reports of board scrutiny.
editorial_case.practical_payoff: Investors and enterprise leaders should monitor the upcoming financial report on November 17 for signs of operational continuity.

stories.headline: Google launches 'Intelligent Eyewear' Android XR glasses
stories.title: Google launches 'Intelligent Eyewear' Android XR glasses
stories.summary: Google has officially opened pre-orders for its new 'Intelligent Eyewear,' a pair of Android XR glasses developed in partnership with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. The glasses feature a 12MP camera, Gemini AI integration for real-time assistance, and privacy-focused features like bystander face redaction and a built-in LED indicator for recording. The glasses are scheduled to begin shipping on December 10, 2026, and represent Google's renewed push into the smart wearable market.
facts: Google's Intelligent Eyewear pre-orders opened on November 12, 2026.
The glasses will ship on December 10, 2026.
They are powered by Google's Android XR platform and Gemini chatbot.
Features include 12MP camera, real-time speech translation, and bystander face redaction.
Privacy controls include a physical on/off switch and a white LED indicator during recording.
Pricing starts at $395 for Warby Parker models and $449-$489 for Gentle Monster versions.
limitations_or_qualifiers: Shipping is initially limited to select markets.
The glasses are designed for specific tasks rather than full-blown mixed reality.
stories.why_it_matters: Google is entering the competitive smart glasses market with a clear focus on privacy and practical agentic AI assistance, challenging existing players like Meta.

editorial_case.new_development: Google opened pre-orders for its first Android XR-powered smart glasses.
editorial_case.affected_listener: Consumers and tech enthusiasts interested in wearable AI are affected.
editorial_case.why_today: The launch marks a significant, public-facing move by Google into a new hardware category that integrates its AI models directly into daily life.
editorial_case.distinct_question: How does Google's approach to wearable privacy and AI assistance compare to Meta's established presence?
editorial_case.new_since_prior_coverage: Pricing, shipping dates, and specific privacy features like face redaction are confirmed today.
editorial_case.practical_payoff: Consumers can now choose between competing ecosystems for wearable AI, with Google emphasizing privacy-first integration.

stories.headline: Meta launches Muse AI assistant for smartwatches
stories.title: Meta launches Muse AI assistant for smartwatches
stories.summary: Meta has released 'Muse,' its latest personal AI assistant, as a native application for Apple Watch and Android Wear OS devices. Unlike desktop or mobile-focused AI models, Muse is optimized for glanceable information, proactive notifications, and voice-based interaction. The assistant integrates with Meta's broader AI ecosystem to provide contextual updates based on user habits and daily schedules.
facts: Meta launched the Muse AI assistant for Apple Watch and Android Wear OS.
Muse is designed for voice interaction and proactive, glanceable information.
It integrates with existing Meta AI platform accounts.
The launch occurred on November 12, 2026.
limitations_or_qualifiers: Feature set is optimized for short, watch-based interactions rather than complex document processing.
Requires active pairing with a smartphone running the Meta app.
stories.why_it_matters: This marks a strategic expansion of AI assistants from the phone screen to the wearable, testing the limits of 'ambient' AI in daily life.

editorial_case.new_development: AI assistants are moving to the wrist, emphasizing 'proactive' and 'glanceable' assistance over complex task completion.
editorial_case.affected_listener: Smartwatch users looking for hands-free, context-aware AI interaction.
editorial_case.why_today: It highlights the industry's shift toward 'ambient' computing, moving AI out of dedicated apps and into background hardware.
editorial_case.distinct_question: Does having an AI assistant on your wrist actually make you more productive, or just more distracted?
editorial_case.new_since_prior_coverage: The arrival of a major agent-style assistant on Wear OS/Apple Watch is new territory for this cycle.
editorial_case.practical_payoff: Evaluate if the proactive nature of Muse solves the 'notification fatigue' problem or adds to it.

stories.headline: Vercel data shows AI model 'half-life' is shrinking to six weeks
stories.title: Vercel data shows AI model 'half-life' is shrinking to six weeks
stories.summary: Data released by Vercel indicates that the 'half-life' of an AI model—the time it takes for a new model to capture significant traffic from its predecessor—is now just six weeks. The report shows that the vast majority of AI production traffic is currently running on models less than two months old, highlighting the breakneck speed of innovation and replacement in the developer ecosystem.
facts: Vercel reported an AI model 'half-life' of six weeks.
Most production AI traffic is currently served by models released within the last two months.
The data tracks the turnover of AI models in web application environments.
The report was published on November 12, 2026.
limitations_or_qualifiers: Based on Vercel platform data, which may be biased toward web-centric, developer-focused applications.
Does not account for non-web-based enterprise AI workloads.
stories.why_it_matters: This evidence challenges the 'stability' narrative of AI infrastructure, showing that businesses are constantly swapping models to maintain performance or cost-efficiency.

editorial_case.new_development: An empirical benchmark has been established for how quickly AI development teams are forced to swap models.
editorial_case.affected_listener: Product managers, engineers, and decision-makers worried about 'lock-in' or the longevity of their AI stack.
editorial_case.why_today: It provides a clear, data-driven answer to whether teams are actually keeping up with the rapid pace of AI model releases.
editorial_case.distinct_question: How can you build a stable long-term product on a foundation that changes or is replaced every six weeks?
editorial_case.new_since_prior_coverage: This is the first quantified metric of 'model churn' in real-world application traffic.
editorial_case.practical_payoff: Teams can use this data to justify building 'model-agnostic' application layers rather than hard-coding dependencies on a single frontier model.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini Decisions API for fast multimodal decision-making
stories.title: Google launches Gemini Decisions API for fast multimodal decision-making
stories.summary: Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API on November 11. The company says the new endpoint is designed for closed-set decisions such as tool selection, policy checks, model routing, and context grading. It says the system can evaluate up to 1,000 questions across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs in a single pass. Google also says the API is available through Gemini API in Google AI Studio and is priced at $0.10 per 1 million input tokens with no output-token billing.
facts: Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API on November 11, 2026.
Google says it is powered by Gemini Decision 1.
The API is designed for bounded decisions such as tool selection, policy checks, model routing, and context grading.
Google says it can process multimodal inputs across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs.
Google says it can evaluate up to 1,000 yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring questions in a single pass.
Google says it is available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.
limitations_or_qualifiers: This is a developer API, not a consumer chat feature.
It is designed for bounded decisions, not open-ended generation.
Pricing and capability claims come from Google’s announcement.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters because it gives builders a new, lower-friction tool for routing and evaluation tasks that sit inside many agent workflows.

editorial_case.new_development: Google added a new decision-focused API intended to speed up multimodal routing and evaluation tasks.
editorial_case.affected_listener: Developers building agents, workflow systems, and moderation or policy tooling are affected.
editorial_case.why_today: It is a concrete product release with access and pricing, not just a benchmark or research note.
editorial_case.distinct_question: What is the Gemini Decisions API for, and how does it differ from a normal model call?
editorial_case.new_since_prior_coverage: This is a new API and pricing model, not a variation of the earlier Carbon release.
editorial_case.practical_payoff: Teams can test whether a specialized decision layer is cheaper and faster than using a general model for routing or policy checks.
